history.message: Baxter agrees to speak with you privately. The officer stays with the others.

“Ms. Dunbar was with me at the concert on the night that Marshall killed himself. She became ill at intermission and hired a car to take her back home. You see, Inspector, I know that Ms. Dunbar appreciates classical music, so I occasionally ask her along to my subscription series. I really should have told the other detective, but I didn't think it mattered.”
The private interview with Baxter ends. Baxter returns to the officer and the group.
Dunbar agrees to speak with you privately. The officer stays with the others.

“Oh, I...well, I guess I should tell you. You see, Mr. Baxter and I, we go together to concerts, only occasionally, you understand. We went that night, the night Marshall died. Then he took me home and that's it. I should have said something before, but I just didn't think it was important, and, well, I didn't think that the others should know we were seeing each other socially. Our...nobody knows about it, you know. Please don't say anything!”
Dunbar consents to the search. You find a bottle of LoBlo among her belongings.
The private interview with Dunbar ends. Dunbar returns to the officer and the group.
George agrees to speak with you privately. The officer stays with the others.
“I haven't a clue.”

“I don't know much about that.”

You enter the kitchen.
Each piece is hand-painted with a scene from Greek mythology.
There are six hand-painted cups and seven hand-painted saucers in the cabinet.
There are eight large and small plates, seven saucers, and six cups.
You enter the garden.
There are two holes in the soft earth, each about two inches by four inches and at least three inches deep. The soil around them is compacted.
The wooden ladder is about fifteen feet long and caked with dirt and dried mud. Its feet seem to fit the holes in the garden.
Digging in the soft earth, you cut your finger on a sharp edge and find a piece of porcelain covered in dirt and dried mud.
The porcelain fragment is covered in dried mud, with its design difficult to make out.
As you wipe off the porcelain, its hand-painted design becomes visible. The markings match the china you examined in the Kitchen.
The lab finds traces of tea and sugar, along with another chemical not commonly used as medication. It is not Amitraxin (Ebullion). No clear fingerprints remain.

“Dear Leslie,

I am sorry to hear that Marshall is despondent again. I know how much his troubles weigh on you, and I wish I could be there to comfort you. His despondency is tied to his business. He speaks of suicide when he is in this state, but the thought of what will happen to the company may keep him going.

So George has made his threats again? It is hard to believe he could cause Marshall so much pain. If the worst should happen, you will be provided for as you deserve.
